summary: Adversarial pass over the SCHED-4B plan (prompt-on-pause + setup story + drained recovery + lifecycle honesty + provider parity). Four findings, three resolved by plan content, one parked as an explicit implementer criterion.
gaps: Route divergence: the setup card goes to the job's notification route while permission prompts go to the authorized approver route; the plan's 'one message carrying story and buttons' claim silently assumes the routes coincide.

The request-only review helper is file-private and expects signed app scope, display/review data and a complete toolInput; the plan says 'lift into an application seam' without stating that the pause path must construct these from the job's stored requirement with host authority (never from channel input).

Allow-once settlement on a dead run: recheckSetupPausedJobsAfterCapabilityUpdate fires on persistent grants; the plan does not state what resumes the job after a transient temporaryOnly approval, so Allow once could approve access yet leave the job paused forever.
contradictions: Roadmap SCHED-4B criterion 1 demands an 'approve-this-requirement affordance rendered and parseable on all providers and preserved through durable enqueue'; the owner-approved prompt-on-pause shape ships the standard prompt's affordances instead of a new card action kind, so a literal reading of the criterion fails.
resolutions: Route divergence: when the approver route differs from the job route, the prompt (story + buttons) goes to the approver route and the job route keeps the instruction-only setup card; when they coincide it is one message. Bound as an explicit decomposition criterion with a test for the divergent-route case.

Seam contract bound into the decomposition: the application seam receives only host-derived inputs (jobId + the job's stored requirement), constructs review/display data itself, and rejects any blocker type it cannot map (falls back to the instruction card); no channel-supplied identifiers ever reach grant construction.

Criterion-1 wording: owner-approved deviation recorded in the plan Risks section and restated in the decomposition objective — the prompt-on-pause affordances ARE the approve-from-card mechanism; the roadmap criterion is satisfied by the standard prompt rendered at pause time on all four providers.
open_items: Allow-once resume semantics parked as a mandatory implementer criterion: after a transient temporaryOnly approval, the job must either be queued for one immediate run through the existing transient-access consumption path, or the receipt must state exactly when the access will be used; silently staying paused is a task failure. The implementer verifies which behavior the existing pendingAccessRequests consumption already provides before choosing.
